overview.summary: ssh (secure shell) provides encrypted remote access to servers and computers. It's the standard way to securely connect to remote Linux systems, execute commands, transfer files, and manage servers. Essential for system administration and remote work.

misconceptions.title: SSH requires password
misconceptions.reality: SSH can use password OR SSH keys. Key-based authentication is more secure and doesn't require typing password. Most servers support both methods.
misconceptions.tip: Set up SSH keys for passwordless, more secure access. Use ssh-keygen to generate keys, ssh-copy-id to copy to server.

misconceptions.title: SSH is only for Linux
misconceptions.misconception: SSH only works with Linux servers
misconceptions.reality: SSH works with Linux, macOS, Windows (with OpenSSH), and many other systems. It's a cross-platform protocol.
misconceptions.tip: SSH works on many platforms. Windows 10+ includes OpenSSH client by default.

common_pitfalls.description: Using wrong username for remote server
common_pitfalls.solution: Verify correct username. Common: root, ubuntu (AWS), ec2-user (Amazon Linux), admin. Check server documentation.

common_pitfalls.description: SSH key file has wrong permissions
common_pitfalls.solution: Set correct permissions: chmod 600 ~/.ssh/key.pem. SSH requires private keys to be readable only by owner.

common_pitfalls.description: Cannot connect - connection refused or timeout
common_pitfalls.solution: Check firewall rules, ensure SSH port (22 or custom) is open. Check server is running SSH daemon (sshd).

best_practices: Use SSH keys instead of passwords for better security
Use ssh-keygen to generate keys, ssh-copy-id to set them up
Set correct permissions on SSH keys: chmod 600 ~/.ssh/key
Use -i to specify key file for cloud instances
Use ssh config file (~/.ssh/config) for easier connections
Type 'exit' or Ctrl+D to disconnect from remote session
performance_tips: Key-based authentication is faster than password (no typing)
SSH compression can speed up connections on slow networks

additional_notes.authentication: SSH supports password and key-based authentication. Keys are more secure and convenient.
additional_notes.default_port: Default SSH port is 22. Many servers change this for security.
additional_notes.ssh_config: Use ~/.ssh/config file to store connection settings (host, user, port, key) for easier access
additional_notes.common_use: Very common: ssh user@server (connect), ssh user@server 'command' (execute), ssh -i key.pem user@server (with key)
